owned_invariants: A patch is a unified diff of existing text files: each file has a --- a/PATH line, a +++ b/PATH line with the same path, and one or more hunks. diff --git and index lines are skipped; any other line outside a hunk is refused.

Creating, deleting, renaming, copying or re-moding a file, /dev/null on either side and binary data are refused as PATCH_SCOPE_REFUSED before any hunk is read. Every other malformed patch is refused as PATCH_REFUSED.
A file may be patched once. A hunk's rows must add up to exactly the two counts its header declares, and old lines are counted from 1.

apply places each hunk at the line its header names, with no offset and no fuzz: every context and removed line must equal the file's line at that position, and hunks must be in order without overlap. Otherwise the whole file's patch is refused and nothing is returned.
Lines the hunks do not touch are returned byte for byte, and a no-newline marker removes the line end of the row before it and of nothing else.
parse and apply read text and return text. Neither touches a file.
boundaries: apply does not decide which files may be patched; the caller compares FilePatch::path with its write set.
Line ends are bytes of the line: a file with CRLF line ends needs a patch written with them.
No rename detection, no three-way merge and no partial application.
